ap.title: Apostilles for U.S. documents going abroad
ap.lead: Tell us where the document was issued and which country needs it. We find the office that issues the apostille, prepare the request and track it, with every cost listed before you pay.
ap.route.title: Where it goes depends on who issued the document
ap.route.lead: There's no single apostille office for every document. We work this out before we send a quote.
ap.route.state.d: Birth and marriage certificates, court records, notarized documents. Usually the Secretary of State of the state that issued or notarized the document.
ap.route.fed.d: For example FBI background checks or other federal records. These go to the U.S. Department of State, not to a state office.
ap.route.foreign.d: An apostille can only be issued in the country where the document was issued. We explain the options and what can be done in the U.S., such as a certified translation.
ap.faq.q1: Does every country accept an apostille?
ap.faq.a1: Only countries that are party to the Hague Apostille Convention. For other countries a different process (legalization through an embassy) applies; we tell you which one fits.
ap.faq.a2: Usually an original or a certified copy issued by the official office is required. A plain photocopy is generally not enough. We confirm the requirement for your document.
ap.faq.a3: It depends on the issuing office and shipping. We give you an estimate with the quote and update you at each step.

nc.lead: We prepare your petition packet from your answers and write out how to file it in your county. Our fee is fixed; the court's fees are listed separately below, so you see the whole cost before you start.

nc.cost.lead: Pick your county. Our fee stays the same; court and background-check fees are paid by you directly to the clerk and to the state.

nc.how.title: How it goes
nc.how.s1.d: Florida requires us to give you a written disclosure first (Form 12.900(a)). Then you answer the questions in writing, in English, Russian or Spanish.
nc.how.s2.d: We type the court-approved forms from your answers and add written filing steps for your county.
nc.how.s3.d: You sign and file with the clerk, pay the court fee and complete the background check.
nc.how.s4.d: The court reviews the petition, usually at a short hearing. After the judgment, our checklist shows where to update your name.
nc.family.title: For a child or a whole family
nc.family.lead: A child's name change usually needs the other parent's consent or formal notice, and a family petition covers several people. We look at your situation first and confirm the price in writing.
nc.faq.q1: Will I have to go to court?
nc.faq.a1: Usually there is a short final hearing in front of a judge. The clerk tells you the date and whether it is in person or by video.
nc.faq.q2: If you were born outside Florida or outside the U.S.
nc.faq.a2: That's fine. You can still file in the Florida county where you live. If your birth certificate is not in English, the court may ask for a certified translation, which we can prepare.
nc.faq.q3: Restoring a former name after a divorce
nc.faq.a3: If your divorce case is still open, the name can often be restored in that case. If it is closed, a separate petition works, and fingerprints are usually not needed to restore a former name.
nc.faq.q4: Can you tell me whether I qualify or what to write?
nc.faq.a4: We prepare the approved forms from your own answers. For advice on your rights, contact an attorney or The Florida Bar Lawyer Referral Service.

fw.meta.desc: Court and USCIS fee waiver forms typed from your written answers: Florida civil indigent status, USCIS I-912, federal in forma pauperis and other states. One fixed price per application; the court or USCIS decides.
fw.title: Can't afford the filing fee? Ask to have it waived.
fw.lead: Courts and USCIS can waive or reduce their fees for people with low income. We type the waiver form from your written answers and list the documents it asks for. One price per application, whichever form it is.
fw.which.title: Which waiver do you need?
fw.which.lead: Each court system has its own form. Tell us where your case is or which USCIS form you're filing.
fw.v.fl.d: Application for civil indigent status, filed with the clerk. Used for court fees in cases such as a name change.
fw.v.uscis.d: Request for a fee waiver on eligible immigration forms, filed together with that form. The I-912 itself has no USCIS fee.
fw.v.fed.d: Application to proceed without prepaying fees (AO 240 or AO 239). The judge decides.
fw.v.other.d: Most state courts have a similar form. Tell us the state and the court, and we'll confirm we can prepare it before you pay.
fw.not.title: Separate services
fw.faq.q1: Can you tell me if I qualify?
fw.faq.a1: The court or USCIS decides. We type the form exactly from your written answers.
fw.faq.q2: What if the waiver is denied?
fw.faq.a2: You can usually still pay the fee and continue, or follow the instructions in the denial. Our fee covers preparing the application, not the decision.
fw.faq.q3: Why is my name on the form as the preparer?
fw.faq.a3: Many waiver forms, including the I-912, require anyone who helped to sign the preparer section. It shows who typed the form; it does not make us your representative.
fw.faq.q4: Can I get the waiver form for a name change too?
fw.faq.a4: Yes. If you are changing your name through a Florida court and can't afford the court fee, the civil indigent application is a separate application at the same fixed price.

bf.lead: Annual reports, trade names, amendments and certificates for Florida companies. We check your Sunbiz record, type the filing and send you the result. State fees are paid at cost.
bf.dl.title: The annual report is due by May 1
bf.dl.text: Florida opens the annual report on January 1. After May 1 the state adds a $400 late fee for LLCs and corporations. That fee goes to the state, not to us. If the report is still not filed, the state can dissolve the company.

bf.faq.a2: We can still file. The state adds its $400 late fee, and we show you the total before you pay. If the company was already dissolved, reinstatement is a separate quote.
bf.faq.q3: Does the yearly plan renew automatically?
bf.faq.a3: No. You pay for one year at a time. Before the next year we ask you, and nothing is charged unless you agree.
bf.faq.q4: Do I need a newspaper notice for a DBA?
bf.faq.a4: Yes. Florida law requires the name to be advertised once in a newspaper in the county of your main place of business before you register. We tell you how, or arrange it at the newspaper’s price.
bf.faq.q5: Can you change the owners or members of my company?

lp.privacy.two_streams.li1: Site data — submissions through public forms, cookies, and optional analytics on vitacorexllc.com. Governed by this privacy policy.
lp.privacy.two_streams.li2: Operator data — data processed during engagements under a signed engagement letter (and, on request, a Data Processing Addendum). Governed by the DPA clauses summarized on the Sub-processors & DPA page and by the operator’s own data-handling requirements where stricter.
lp.privacy.use.li4: Site data is not sold or rented. Where consented analytics (GA4) is active, measurement data is aggregated and retained per the consent banner choices. Operator engagement data is never used for any marketing.
lp.privacy.files.p1: The public forms are designed for general business documents and non-regulated materials. Do not upload highly sensitive regulated records, medical records subject to HIPAA, financial records subject to GLBA, or other materials that require a dedicated secure workflow unless secure coordination has been arranged first. For regulated-data engagements the correct intake path is the Structured Case Intake followed by an engagement letter and, where applicable, a Business Associate Agreement.
lp.privacy.cookies.p1: The site uses a consent banner that distinguishes essential functionality from optional analytics or marketing measurement. Visitors can choose essential only, analytics only, or full consent where available. See the Cookie Policy for the specific cookie inventory.
lp.privacy.marketing.p1: VitaCoreX may upload hashed business-contact email addresses to Google Ads Customer Match for the sole purpose of creating matched audiences for our own advertising on Google Search, Display, and YouTube networks. Hashing is performed before transmission; Google receives a one-way SHA-256 hash, not the plaintext email.
lp.privacy.marketing.li1: Scope: B2B operator contacts only — dental groups, healthcare networks, fleet operators, subscription businesses, contract-services firms, and similar commercial leads. Private-client (immigration, auto, contract review) emails are excluded by policy and never uploaded.
lp.privacy.marketing.li2: Purpose limitation: Audience matching for VitaCoreX advertising only. Google does not use uploaded data for its own advertising or to improve other advertisers’ targeting. Hashed data is retained by Google only for the matching process and is deleted when the list is removed or expires.
lp.privacy.marketing.li3: Lawful basis: Legitimate interests in B2B advertising (GDPR Art. 6(1)(f) where applicable). For US contacts, processing is consistent with CCPA business-purpose use; we do not “sell” personal information as defined by CCPA.
lp.privacy.marketing.li4: Right to opt out: Email info@vitacorexllc.com with the subject “Customer Match Opt-Out” to be permanently excluded from any current or future marketing-audience uploads. Removal from existing Google audiences typically takes 7 days.
lp.privacy.marketing.li5: Sub-processor: Google LLC (Mountain View, CA, USA) acts as our processor under the Google Ads Data Processing Terms for Customer Match data.
lp.privacy.third_parties.p1: Form delivery, calendar scheduling, analytics, email infrastructure, CRM, document signature, and optional campaign measurement rely on named third-party services. The complete list — vendor, purpose, data categories touched, and region — is published on the Sub-processors & DPA page and is updated when vendors are added, changed, or removed (30-day standard notice; 15-day objection window; 5-day emergency notice for security-driven swaps).
lp.privacy.operator_data.p1: Applies to engagement data, not site data. Operator data processed during engagements is used only for the purposes named in the engagement letter. It is not repurposed for marketing, training of general-purpose AI models, or use on other engagements. Operator data stays isolated in engagement-scoped storage with access limited to the named engagement team.
lp.privacy.retention.p1: Site data: form submissions are retained while the inquiry is open plus 36 months for pattern analysis, then aggregated or deleted. Analytics data follows the GA4 default 14-month window unless you opt out.
lp.privacy.retention.p2: Operator data: default retention is engagement duration plus 90 days unless the operator requests extended retention in writing. Certificates of destruction are issued at close and list what was destroyed and the method used. Operator-environment engagements require no destruction action on our side — access is revoked at close. Full retention matrix on the Security & Compliance page.
lp.privacy.breach.p1: If VitaCoreX becomes aware of a personal-data or operator-data breach, the affected operator (for engagement data) or the affected individual (for site data, where individual notice is appropriate) is notified without undue delay and in no case later than 72 hours of becoming aware. Notification includes scope of data affected, systems affected, initial containment actions, and a named point of contact for the remediation thread. See the incident-response posture on the Security & Compliance page and the DPA clause on the Sub-processors & DPA page.
lp.privacy.rights.p2: Submit requests to (888) 794-8292 or through the contact form with subject line “privacy request.” Standard response time is 10 business days; verification of requester identity may be required for non-trivial requests. For engagement data, requests run through the operator (data controller) rather than VitaCoreX directly.
lp.privacy.transfers.p1: All site data and all operator data are stored and processed on US-based infrastructure with US-based cloud vendors. No client or site data is stored in, processed in, or transits through jurisdictions outside the United States in ordinary operation. If a future engagement requires a different posture, it is documented in the engagement letter with the controlling transfer mechanism named in writing.
lp.privacy.contact.p1: Privacy-related questions: contact form (subject line “privacy”) or call/text (888) 794-8292. Procurement contacts can also reach the designated procurement point of contact named in the engagement letter.
